item.title: Standing AI Adoption Policy
item.body_md:
## How to use this template

Replace every bracketed field. Delete any clause that does not apply rather than leaving it aspirational: a policy that promises review you do not perform is worse than no policy, because it documents a control you have failed.

This is a template, not legal advice. Have counsel review before adoption if your sector carries specific obligations.

---

## 1. Purpose

[ORGANISATION] uses artificial intelligence tools in the course of its work. This policy states which tools are approved, what may and may not be done with them, and how an employee requests something not on the list. It applies to every employee, contractor, and volunteer, on any device, for any work product.

The policy exists so that the answer to "was this allowed?" is always available before the fact rather than reconstructed after an incident.

## 2. Scope

This policy covers any system that generates, summarises, classifies, translates, or recommends using a machine-learning model, whether purchased, subscribed to, embedded in another product, or free. It covers use in a browser tab as much as use in an integrated system. Personal accounts used for work purposes are in scope; work accounts used for personal purposes are out of scope but not thereby permitted.

## 3. Approved tools

| Tool | Approved for | Not approved for | Data classification permitted | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [TOOL] | [TASKS] | [TASKS] | [PUBLIC / INTERNAL / CONFIDENTIAL] | [NAME] |

Any tool not on this table is unapproved. Unapproved is not the same as forbidden: it means the request path in section 6 has not yet been followed.

## 4. Conditions of use

1. **Data.** Do not enter [CLASSIFICATION] or above into any tool whose row above does not permit it. This includes customer records, personnel matters, unreleased financials, credentials, and anything received under an obligation of confidence.
2. **Verification.** AI output is a draft. The person who submits work is accountable for it, whatever produced it. Verify facts, figures, citations, and quotations against a source before the work leaves your hands.
3. **Disclosure.** Disclose AI assistance where [ORGANISATION] has told a client, regulator, or counterparty that it would, and wherever the recipient would reasonably expect a human author.
4. **Attribution and licence.** Do not represent AI output as the work of a named individual who did not write it. Respect the licence terms of any material you supply as input.
5. **Prohibited uses.** No AI tool may be used to make a final decision about hiring, dismissal, discipline, credit, pricing to an individual, or eligibility for a benefit or service. Those decisions require a named human owner who can explain the reasoning without reference to a model.

## 5. Records

Where an AI tool contributes materially to a decision or a deliverable, record: the tool, the date, the person accountable, and what was verified. [SYSTEM] is the record location. Retain for [PERIOD].

## 6. Requesting a new tool

Send [OWNER] the tool name, vendor, what you want to use it for, what data it would see, and the vendor's terms and privacy page. [OWNER] responds within [N] working days with approved, approved with conditions, or declined and why. Approved tools are added to the table in section 3, which is republished on approval rather than at a review cycle.

## 7. Review

[OWNER] reviews this policy every [PERIOD] and whenever a tool in section 3 materially changes its terms, its data handling, or its model. The review date and the reviewer are recorded on the policy itself.

## 8. Breach

Report suspected breaches to [OWNER]. Reporting your own mistake promptly is treated as compliance with this policy, not as a breach of it. Concealment is the breach.

---

**Version [N] · Adopted [DATE] · Owner [NAME] · Next review [DATE]**
item.summary: An always-on policy stating which AI tools and uses are approved, on what conditions, and how someone requests a new one. Replaces case-by-case improvisation with a standing rule set that survives staff turnover.
item.audience: Any organisation with staff using AI tools, whether or not it has approved them
